source_metadata.etymology_text: Borrowed from German Bass or French basse. The meaning “prison” was probably based on French au violon (“in prison”, literally “in violin”). The meaning “bottle crate” was probably derived from that, with the bottles being confined in the crate. First attested in the 17th century.
raw_glosses: (informal, expressive) prison (a place of long-term confinement for those convicted of serious crimes)
